title: Research: sixteen-array transcript floor survives QQ16 selected shears
body:
An invertible A-to-T shear between QQ16's complete F0 and B1 calls still leaves a quantified information deficit. With the retained local maps and ordinary tail, an additional rational-linear record of total rank d leaves at least `ceil(77N/5)-d` dimensions of original joint A/T input invisible. One dense eight-coordinate query leaves at least `ceil(37N/5)`; fifteen uniform scalar owner arrays are insufficient, so sixteen are necessary. Sufficiency is open. The necessary unrestricted total rank is `ceil(77N/5)`, not `16N`.

Only `research/qq16-shear-transcript-floor/` is added. The package contains the ordered proof, exact source pins, a separate fourth-moment implementation, noncommuting rational fixtures, the retained logical tail, and read-only replay with corruption controls.

### Scope and overlap

The decoder gets all post-B1 selected cuts, later homogeneous selected-only controls, five forward histories and completed-X descendants. Pre-B1 selected transients must be counted in d; the former-Y endpoint is excluded. Record-driven paired updates vanish when the record is zero. The ordinary fields and retained local maps stay fixed.

Concurrent **#2368** (`e5d4d78dcfdd55d323fcbc60df477b9f25c7abff`) independently proves the overlapping B0-read obstruction using the second moment, and also permits invertible pairings. Its written proof was read during publication; its kernel is equivalent on that restriction. This contribution adds the arbitrary rank-d record bound, the stronger fourth-moment deficit and sixteen-array floor, and a separate exact text-source moment checker. No first-closure claim. The original package was committed locally at 06:08 UTC before reading #2368.

**#2189** supplies the credited fourth moment and rank bound `117N/5`; that numerical result is reused, not claimed as new. **#2326** supplied the dense-query handoff. **#2354** concerns the coordinate threshold of its specified common-axis family, while **#2346** excludes early selected intervention and has a different final-only contract.

### Validation

Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12.3, standard library:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/qq16-shear-transcript-floor
```

Registered normal and optimized replay passed in the publication checkout: 18 mathematical/schedule failure controls and five integration tests, including Git-free read-only relocation, source drift, receipt type corruption and overwrite refusal. Checks include 336 owner routes, six 9,216-product tables, exact moments `24,28,109/3,1823/36`, the spectral certificate, full-input fixture kernels and the 17-event tail. Patch application, metadata/source pins and whitespace checks pass. Separate agent reviews found no substantive blocker; no human or hosted-CI pass is claimed.

Hosted workflows currently report `action_required`; the [registered-package run](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38696592489) awaits maintainer approval before execution.

The theorem uses the written rank argument; finite fixtures do not replace it. Compressed packets, native field types/words and full supplier cold replay were not run. The selected-baseline orientation command was attempted in the initial bounded export and could not verify its complete inventory; no baseline pass is claimed. No native tariff, supplier admission or new κ is claimed.

Base and publication refresh: canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. Refreshed overlap covered 584 open PRs including drafts and 1,112 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings. Details and exact heads are in TASK.json.

[Canonical finding and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2205#discussioncomment-18943100).

Credit Ali Romman, commdata2338, @starship-s, Adam Gall, CubeJerry, Cinna Davis, Nick Petalas, Ross Richardson, Charles Bethin, Brody Arbon and the retained construction lineage in the README/NOTICE references. Prepared for Jason (@jgilfoil) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, checking and writing. New work Apache-2.0.
